chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the menstruating woman: what is the limit of her waiting? He said: “She waits for the number of days she used to menstruate, then she exercises precaution for three days, then after that she is in istiḥāḍah.”
So its meaning is what we have mentioned, and that indicates this.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she takes an additional precautionary period
key_terms.جُلُوسِهَا: her remaining seated from acts requiring ritual purity, meaning the period she refrains
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman in the state of istiḥāḍah, irregular bleeding distinct from hayd

ai.seo_question: How long should a menstruating woman wait before being considered in istiḥāḍah according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the duration a menstruating woman remains in the state of hayd. It states that she counts the days of her usual menstruation, then adds three precautionary days, after which she is considered mustaḥāḍah. The report is relevant to the rulings of ritual purity and acts of worship.
